symptom: describe → exec dropped the design properties stored on a page itself (Forms$Page Appearance.DesignProperties): native pages lost 'Spacing top': 'Inner large', 'Spacing bottom': 'Inner large', 'Background color': 'Background Primary'. describe printed none in the header, exec wrote an empty list, and a page-level `alter page … set ('Background color': …)` was refused as 'unsupported page-level property'
cause: MDL had no page-level spelling: the page header grammar had no DesignProperties, pages.Page no field, pageToGen passed nil to newAppearance, describe's header read only Class and Style, and page-level SET routed every key to applyPageLevelSetMut
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLPage.g4 (pageHeaderPropertyV3); mdl/visitor/visitor_page_v3.go; mdl/executor/cmd_pages_builder_v3.go (buildPageV3), cmd_pages_describe.go (page header); mdl/backend/modelsdk/page_write.go (pageToGen); mdl/executor/theme_reader.go (pageThemeKey: Document + Page groups); design_property_routing.go + mdl/backend/pagemutator/mutator.go (findStyleableWidget("") is the page); validate_design_properties.go
fix: Add `DesignProperties: ( … )` to the page header, typed against the theme's Document and Page groups after the layout fixes the platform; describe prints it; page-level `alter page … set ('Key': value)` writes the page's own Appearance; check -p validates the header
insight: The values looked like a custom theme until every design-properties.json was grepped for the key across ALL groups: Atlas Core's native file has a 'Document' group no widget type is named after, and it holds exactly the reported values. Grep by property name, not by the group you expect. Which groups a page takes was settled by mxbuild, not by reading: a page-level 'Spacing left': 'Small' (valid in Widget, not in Document) is CE6085 'Unknown option Small', so a page takes Document and not Widget — including Widget made check warn on the reporter's own values
